spatial_claims.claim: C lies between A and B on straight line AB (collinear arrangement for segment subtraction)

configuration_map: Minimal configuration: a straight line AB with point C between A and B, creating segments AC and BC. No further geometric constructions are made. The entire proof operates on areas (sum of squares S, twice rectangle T) and their commensurability relationships, with no spatial reasoning beyond the initial collinear setup.
skip_reason: The proof is purely algebraic/area-theoretic. It deals with medial areas, rational areas, and their arithmetic relationships (via II.7 and X.26). The only spatial element is the trivial collinearity of A, C, B on a line segment, which is the standard setup for subtraction and involves no geometric configuration that could be contradictory. No angle decompositions, no interior/exterior arguments, no circle relationships, and no ray orderings appear anywhere in the proof.
